newsitem.title: CANADA: Petro-Canada aiming for higher gas returns.
newsitem.headline: Petro-Canada aiming for higher gas returns.

text.p: Petro-Canada is aiming to boost returns from its growing natural gas production and gain a bigger sales area with its alliance with megamarketer Enron Corp, a Petro-Canada spokesman said on Wednesday.

"It is expected to maximize the netback from our natural gas volumes and achieve that through a better understanding and better ability to access the U.S. market," Petro-Canada's Bill Simpkins said. "It also will help in optimizing our transportation and storage commitments."

Petro-Canada, Canada's second largest gas producer with current output of 840 million cubic feet per day, on Wednesday announced an alliance with Houston-based Enron, which would market its gas natural gas production and provide financial and risk management services.
Simpkins said the deal differed from rival Suncor Inc's marketing deal with Enron, announced in October, because Petro-Canada was maintaining its ability to market gas by doing its own deals.
Petro-Canada's gas marketing department currently has 12 staff and most were expected to continue working in other parts of the company, he said.
The savings expected as part of the deal were not being disclosed for competitive reasons, Simpkins said.
However, he said a one cent improvement in the company's natural gas netback had a before-tax impact on earnings of C$3 million.
The deal, currently in the memorandum of understanding stage, was expected to close shortly, he said.
Petro-Canada's natural gas production gre by 40 percent last year, mostly from its acquisition of Amerada Hess Canada.
